title: CareShield Life and Long-Term Care (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: CareShield Life and Long-Term Care (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: CareShield Life payout growth doubled
sections.summary: The Council recommended doubling CareShield Life payout growth from 2% to 4% annually, so a 2030 claim pays $806 monthly instead of $731.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Notably, the Council recommended doubling of the growth rate of CareShield Life payouts from 2% to 4% annually.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: With this enhancement, a policyholder making a claim in 2030 will receive $806 per month, compared to $731 per month under the previous annual growth rate.

sections.label: Government premium support commitment
sections.summary: The Government committed over $570 million in additional support over five years, moderating annual premium increases from 2026 to 2030 to about $38 on average and no more than $75.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: To help policyholders cope with the premium adjustments, the Government has also committed to providing over $570 million in additional support over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: This will moderate annual premium increases from 2026 to 2030 to about $38 on average and no more than $75.

sections.label: Optional Cohort enrolment as of June 2025
sections.summary: As of June 2025, about 900,000, or almost half of them, have done so.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: As of June 2025, about 900,000, or almost half of them have done so.

sections.label: Reinstating Optional Cohort underwriting criteria
sections.summary: The CareShield Life Council recommended reinstating the planned underwriting criteria for the Optional Cohorts from 1 January 2026 onwards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: This indicates that most Optional Cohort individuals who wanted to enrol have done so.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Hence, the CareShield Life Council has recommended reinstating the planned underwriting criteria for the Optional Cohorts from 1 January 2026 onwards.

sections.label: Merdeka Generation premium reduction example
sections.summary: A CareShield Life policyholder from the Merdeka Generation born in 1952 would see annual premiums lower by more than $100 in 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: For instance, a CareShield Life policyholder from the Merdeka Generation born in 1952 would see annual premiums lower by more than $100 in 2026.

sections.label: New citizens enrolment disability condition
sections.summary: From 1 January 2026, these new Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents can only enrol in CareShield Life if they are not disabled.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: From 1 January 2026, these new Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents can only enrol in CareShield Life if they are "not disabled".

sections.label: Premium subsidies and support
sections.summary: The Government provides premium subsidies and transitional support, and Additional Premium Support fully offsets remaining premiums for those unable to afford them.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: We also recognise that premiums must be kept affordable, especially for those who are vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: This is why the Government provides support in the form of premium subsidies for lower- and middle-income households and has also announced transitional support to help policyholders manage the upcoming round of premium adjustments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Additional Premium Support is also available to fully offset the remainder of the premiums for those who remain unable to afford their premiums even after subsidies and have limited family support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: So, here, I want to emphasise that no one will lose CareShield Life coverage due to an inability to pay premiums, because from what I just said, those in the worst and most dire situations who cannot afford to even pay the premiums after our subsidies, the Government will step in and pay fully whatever is left for them to bear.

sections.label: Unrecovered premiums borne by policyholders
sections.summary: Unrecovered premiums will be shouldered by other policyholders within their cohorts as higher premiums.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Consequently, such unrecovered premiums will have to be shouldered by other policyholders within their cohorts in the form of higher premiums.

sections.label: Demand notes via digital means
sections.summary: Clause 5 allows demand notes to be served via additional modalities such as digital means, on top of existing methods like physical letters.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Clause 5 will enhance our premium recovery efforts by allowing demand notes to be served via additional modalities, such as digital means, on top of existing methods, such as physical letters.

sections.label: Lifetime severe disability risk
sections.summary: One in two residents is expected to develop severe disability in their lifetime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: As the Minister mentioned, one in two residents is expected to develop severe disability in their lifetime.

sections.label: Doubling payout growth
sections.summary: The move to double the payout growth to 4% is welcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: The move to double the payout growth to 4% is welcome.

sections.label: Long duration severe disability
sections.summary: While the median disability duration is about four years, three in 10 Singaporeans could remain severely disabled for 10 years or more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: While I understand the median disability duration is about four years, there are three in 10 Singaporeans that could remain severely disabled for 10 years or more.

sections.label: MediSave premium increase impact
sections.summary: The 4% annual premium increase, especially after transitional subsidies taper off by 2030, can add up and eat into MediSave balances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: The 4% annual premium increase, especially after transitional subsidies taper off by 2030, can add up and eat into MediSave balances.

sections.label: CareShield Life scheme improvements
sections.summary: The passage urges that payouts cover a certain percent of long-term care costs, premiums be capped at a fixed percentage of median per capita household income, and caregivers receive support, including possible CPF top-ups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: While strengthening this scheme, we must also ensure that it truly benefits those in need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: We can approach this from three aspects: (a) that payouts can cover at least a certain percent of estimated long-term care costs – giving families predictability to plan for their needs; (b) that premiums will remain within reach, by capping premiums at a fixed percentage of the median per capita household income; and (c) that caregivers receive the support they need so that they will be cared for even as they care for their loved ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to consider providing CPF top-ups to primary caregivers who lack retirement savings due to caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: We have an obligation to care for them when they are in need and be their support. : Mr Deputy Speaker, CareShield Life is a key pillar of our nation's approach to long-term care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: It rests on the promise that when one pays premiums faithfully through the working years, one can count on meaningful support when severe disability arise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: As we strengthen the scheme, let us make sure it better delivers the assurance that: payouts can cover at least X percent of estimated long-term care costs, giving families predictability to plan for their needs; that premiums will remain within reach by capping premiums at a fixed percentage of the median per-capita household income; and that caregivers receive the support they need so that they will be cared for even as they care for their loved ones now.

sections.label: Long-term care cost estimates
sections.summary: Even with payouts for the severely disabled, long-term care costs remain significant, with 2024 numbers indicating home-based care can cost $1,800 to $2,500 a month and institutional care $2,200 to $4,200 a month before subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even with payouts for the severely disabled, costs for long-term care are still significant, with 2024 numbers indicating that it can cost on average between $1,800 to $2,500 a month for home-based long-term care, depending on care intensity and subsidies, rising to an estimated average amount of $2,200 to $4,200 a month before subsidies for institutional-based care, such as in a nursing home.

sections.label: Gender pay and CPF gaps
sections.summary: The Ministry of Manpower's 2023 report found women earn 14.3% less than men on a gross basis, with an adjusted gap of 6%, and CPF Board data shows women's balances at age 55 are approximately 55% lower than men's.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Manpower's 2023 Gender Pay Gap report found that women earn 14.3% less than men on a gross basis, with an adjusted gap of 6% still.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: CPF Board data also shows that women's balances at age 55 are approximately 55% lower than men's.

sections.label: Women's poor health years
sections.summary: Studies show women spend about 12% more of their lives in poor health than men.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Studies show they spend about 12% more of their lives in poor health than men.

sections.label: Financial penalty for women
sections.summary: Women could be perceived to be penalised financially for living longer and providing the majority of unpaid care.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Women could be perceived to be penalised financially for two things they cannot control: living longer and providing the majority of unpaid care.

sections.label: Longevity gap between men and women
sections.summary: The longevity gap between men and women has narrowed over two decades from about six years to around 4.4 years today.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Additionally, the longevity gap between men and women has narrowed over the last two decades from about six years, to around 4.4 years today.

sections.label: Underwriting criteria for pre-1980 births
sections.summary: The Bill reinstates underwriting criteria for those born before 1980, so those with severe pre-existing disabilities could no longer sign up.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One of the changes in this Bill too is the reinstating of the underwriting criteria for those born before 1980, which means those with severe pre-existing disabilities would no longer be able to sign up for the scheme.

sections.label: Caregivers at risk of depression
sections.summary: A 2023 survey found over 40% of Singapore caregivers are at risk of depression, typically married women aged 45 to 60 in full-time work.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A 2023 survey found that more than 40% of caregivers in Singapore are at risk of depression.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The typical caregiver is a married woman between the ages of 45 and 60, simultaneously holding down full-time employment, spending an average of an extra 6.7 hours on caregiving a day.

sections.label: CareShield Life founding purpose and goals
sections.summary: After the ElderShield to CareShield Life transition, the next step is ensuring premiums grow transparently and remain affordable, with gender differences reviewed and caregivers supported.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To conclude, Mr Deputy Speaker, after our transition from ElderShield to CareShield Life, the next step is to ensure that CareShield Life remains true to its founding purpose: to stand beside every Singaporean in times of need.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This means ensuring premiums grow transparently and remain affordable, gender-based differences are regularly reviewed as our care needs and demography changes, and caregivers are given training, respite and recognition beyond financial means.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Let us continue towards our goal of a system that reflects our shared values of fairness, inclusion and solidarity, so that every Singaporean, regardless of gender, income or circumstance, is able to live and age with dignity and support.

sections.label: Severe disability among healthy seniors
sections.summary: MOH estimates that half of healthy Singaporeans aged 65 will develop severe disability in their lifetimes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: MOH estimates that half of healthy Singaporeans aged 65 will develop severe disability in their lifetimes.

sections.label: Aligned income thresholds from 2026
sections.summary: From 2026, income thresholds for nursing home subsidies, Home Caregiving Grant and Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund align at $4,800 per capita household income.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: From 2026, the income threshold for nursing home subsidies, Home Caregiving Grant and the Seniors’ Mobility and Enabling Fund will all be aligned at $4,800 per capita household income, and the severe disability assessment for CareShield Life will also apply the Home Caregiving Grant.

sections.label: Premium increases with support
sections.summary: Premiums will rise, with annual increases averaging $38 and up to $75 during transition, or $126 without support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: With this Bill, premiums will rise, even with means tested premium subsidies, transitional support and additional premium support, the annual premium increase will be $38 on average but can go up to $75 during the transitional period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Without support, the average increase would be $126 annually.

sections.label: Risk-sharing for vulnerable groups
sections.summary: The passage asks whether risk-sharing models could protect vulnerable groups, including seniors excluded by reinstated underwriting criteria.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Could we explore risk-sharing models that protect vulnerable groups without overburdening the rest?

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There is a group we must not forget – seniors who are now excluded with the reinstatement of the underwriting criteria.

sections.label: Expanding IDAPE fallback schemes
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry will consider expanding and extending IDAPE or similar fallback schemes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry consider expanding and extending IDAPE or similar fallback schemes?

sections.label: Nursing home wait times
sections.summary: Nationally, the median wait for a nursing home space is four to six weeks, and longer for dementia care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Nationally, the median wait time for a nursing home space is four to six weeks, and longer for dementia care.

sections.label: Goals for ageing society
sections.summary: The passage lists goals: system coherence, affordability, adequate payouts, generational fairness, plugging seniors' coverage gaps and delivering promised care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: To serve our ageing society well, we must build greater system coherence, keep the system affordable and payouts adequate, ensure fairness across generations, plug the coverage gaps for seniors and make sure the care we promise actually gets delivered where and when it is needed.

sections.label: Clause 3 automatic enrollment
sections.summary: Clause 3 amends section 6(1)(b) to automatically enroll certain new Citizens or Permanent Residents not already severely disabled.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clause 3 amends section 6(1)(b) to automatically enroll new Citizens or Permanent Residents born before 1980, or who those who became Citizens or Permanent Residents after October 2020, so long as the individual was not already severely disabled.

sections.label: ADL criteria for CareShield Life
sections.summary: Clauses 7 and 8 formalise six ADLs requiring maximal or total assistance in three for severe disability and CareShield Life payouts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clauses 7 and 8 formalise the six ADLs, for which an individual must require either maximal or total assistance in three, before they are considered severely disabled and, thereby, qualify for CareShield Life payouts.

sections.label: Six ADLs incomplete representation
sections.summary: The six ADLs remain an incomplete representation of an individual's ability to function adequately in a modern community.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Perhaps more important is that these six ADLs remain an incomplete representation of an individual's ability to function adequately in a modern community.

sections.label: Assistance level versus activity count
sections.summary: A concern is whether maximal or total assistance in three activities indicates severe disability more than moderate assistance in five activities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A related concern is whether the need for maximal or total assistance in three activities is more reflective or indicative of severe disability than, say, moderate assistance but in five distinct activities?

sections.label: Sixty-day free-look period
sections.summary: One issue is whether the 60-day free-look period may be too brief for enrollees to decide on remaining permanently.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One issue is whether the 60-day "free-look" period may be too brief for those who enroll to decide on whether they wish to remain on the scheme permanently.

sections.label: Premium support and scheme administration
sections.summary: Questions ask what proportion receive premium support, how to access additional support, and whether CPF Board or a private insurer administers CareShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry clarify what proportion of current participants receive premium support, and what the process of accessing additional premium support entails?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Third, I would like to know whether, in practice, CareShield Life will be directly run by the CPF Board under the direction of the Ministry of Health, or if it will be outsourced to a third-party private insurer, such as Income Insurance, to administer.

sections.label: CPF Board correspondence if outsourced
sections.summary: If CareShield Life is outsourced to a private insurer, correspondence should still come from CPF Board or feature its logo prominently.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For this reason, I believe that it would be useful to ensure that, should CareShield Life ultimately be outsourced to a private insurer for administration, that correspondence pertaining to the scheme still come directly from CPF Board or, at the very least, feature a CPF Board logo prominently in the letterhead.

sections.label: CareShield Life 2025 Review changes
sections.summary: The Government accepted CareShield Life Council recommendations for higher payouts and $575 million in additional premium subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In August 2025, the Government accepted the CareShield Life Council’s recommendations for the 2025 Review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: These include higher payouts to meet long-term care needs and a $575 million in additional premium subsidies to cushion the increase for households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: These changes ensure that CareShield Life remains financially sustainable while protecting Singaporeans who develop severe disabilities from being left behind.

sections.label: Premium stability question
sections.summary: A member asks how stable premiums will remain as payouts rise and the population ages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The additional subsidies is commendable, but as payouts rise and our population ages, how stable will premiums remain over the longer term?

sections.label: Bill support and CareShield refinements
sections.summary: The Bill clarifies coverage and administration, laying groundwork for enhanced CareShield Life benefits from 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: By 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be aged 65 or above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The CareShield Life Scheme is a key pillar of our response to this demographic transformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This Bill is not merely about technical amendments, but it is about how families experience vulnerability, care and experience dignity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I therefore support this Bill and I believe the suggestions that I raised today can make a good Bill even better.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: It clarifies who qualifies for coverage and strengthens how the scheme is administered and communicated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: These refinements lay the groundwork for enhanced benefits for CareShield Life from 2026, including higher monthly payouts and moderated premium increases, ensuring that long-term care for severe disabilities remains accessible and fair.

sections.label: Underwriting criterion for Optional Group
sections.summary: The Bill proposes reinstating the underwriting criterion for the Optional Group to moderate premiums for older policy holders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes the reinstatement of the underwriting criterion for the Optional Group to moderate premium for older policy holders.

sections.label: CareShield Life enrolment figures
sections.summary: 1.9 million Singapore Residents joined CareShield Life, with 900,000 Optional Cohort members opting in.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Since the launch of CareShield Life, as the Senior Minister of State has shared, 1.9 million Singapore Residents have joined the scheme with 900,000 of them, or half of that population of the Optional Cohort opting in.

sections.label: Transitional support and means testing
sections.summary: Transitional support moderates premium increases, while property annual value means testing affects other long-term care schemes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Several of my residents in Changi Simei do fall under this category.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: And the temporary transitional support for CareShield Life which is not means-tested is definitely welcome as it applies to all policy holders and it will moderate the premium increase to $38 per year on average and capped at $75 per year on average and can be fully paid by MediSave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I have called for long-term care policies and support to remain inclusive and responsive to our rapidly ageing population as long-term care is not a one-off but it is an ongoing expense, including premiums.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: So, based on the current means-testing criteria, if a household has no household income, the annual value (AV) of the home is used as the criterion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The means testing criterion of AV of property applies not just to CareShield Life but to other long-term care schemes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Hence, those who fall in this category are not just impacted by higher premium for CareShield Life but eligibility for support of other long-term care schemes including MediSave Care, Home Caregiving Grant and the Elder Fund.

sections.label: Tiering AV threshold by age
sections.summary: Asks whether MOH would tier the AV threshold by age and count household caregiving needs in assessment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Would MOH consider, for example, tiering the AV threshold by age, adjusting the AV cut-off for older cohorts who own only one property?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In using AV as a criterion, can the number of those requiring caregiving and living in the household be a factor for assessment?

sections.label: Underwriting criteria for Optional Cohorts
sections.summary: States that planned underwriting criteria for Optional Cohorts born before 1980 will be reinstated as part of enhancements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As part of the enhancements, the planned underwriting criteria for Optional Cohorts born before 1980 will be reinstated.

sections.label: CareShield Life premium support and sustainability
sections.summary: Notes CareShield Life must stay viable, welcomes $570 million premium support, and notes no one loses coverage for inability to pay.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It is crucial that CareShield Life remains financially viable and sustainable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I can understand that the proposed annual increase in both payout growth rate and premiums from 2026 to 2030 can help to ensure that the scheme keeps pace with inflation and rising care costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I understand that this enhancement will be reviewed after 2030, but it will be difficult to imagine that premiums will not continue to rise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am assured by the Government's commitment of over $570 million in additional premium support to offset more than 30% of the premium increase over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: These Government subsidies for the premiums, especially for the lower-income groups, enhance affordability and ensure majority participation in the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am also glad to note that the Government has reiterated that no one will lose coverage due to their inability to pay their premiums.

sections.label: Government acceptance of council recommendations
sections.summary: Says the Government's acceptance of council recommendations and $570 million premium support show commitment to protecting Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Government's acceptance of the council's recommendations, along with a substantial $570 million commitment in premium support over five years, clearly shows the depth of commitment to protecting Singaporeans.

sections.label: Projected individuals outside CareShield Life coverage
sections.summary: Asks how many individuals are projected to fall outside CareShield Life coverage due to the Bill's revised stipulations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: First, how many individuals are projected to fall outside the scope of CareShield Life coverage due to the revised stipulations set out in this Bill?

sections.label: Transitional support for disqualified individuals
sections.summary: Asks what transitional provisions or support exist for individuals who no longer qualify, and notes enhanced payouts growing to over $800 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Lastly, what transitional provisions or support mechanisms, if any, are in place or contemplated for individuals who no longer qualify because of this legislative change?

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am heartened by the Government's commitment that enhanced payouts will grow from $731 monthly in 2026, to over $800 by 2030, providing meaningful relief to families facing the profound and persistent challenges of severe disability.

sections.label: Dementia prevalence among seniors
sections.summary: One in 10 seniors above 60 in Singapore lives with dementia, projected to exceed 150,000 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Current estimates suggest that one in 10 seniors above 60 in Singapore lives with dementia, and this number is projected to reach well over 150,000 by 2030.

sections.label: Clinical diagnosis triggering CareShield Life
sections.summary: A clinical dementia diagnosis could trigger automatic base-tier CareShield Life eligibility, with functional assessment determining higher-tier payouts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: While clinical evaluation is important, this additional step can cause delay, uncertainty and emotional stress for families already struggling with care arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I propose that these patients already have a clinical diagnosis of dementia and this could be used to trigger automatic base-tier eligibility under CareShield Life, with subsequent functional assessment determining higher-tier payouts.

sections.label: Acute psychiatric beds and eligibility
sections.summary: The Government plans 500 acute psychiatric beds by 2040, with eligibility based on chronicity, treatability and functional impairment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The Government's plans to add 500 acute psychiatric beds by 2040 already underpin the burden of mental illness in our society.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Eligibility for this could be based on three factors: chronicity of disease, treatability and degree of functional impairment.

sections.label: Unified online caregiver platform
sections.summary: A unified online platform could let caregivers view eligibility, submit documentation, receive updates and access schemes such as AIC support services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: A unified online platform, perhaps integrated into current existing platforms, could allow caregivers to view eligibility status, submit documentation, receive updates and access related schemes, such as AIC support services.

sections.label: Integrating CareShield Life and schemes
sections.summary: The Ministry is urged to deepen integration between CareShield Life, AIC, Silver Support and Healthier SG so support reaches families seamlessly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The emotional and financial toll is significant and while CareShield Life helps with the costs, it does not yet address the broader ecosystem of caregivers' needs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to deepen integration and interaction between CareShield Life, the AIC, Silver Support and Healthier SG initiatives, so that financial, emotional and respite support reach families seamlessly.

sections.label: CareShield Life as care framework
sections.summary: CareShield Life should evolve from a financial safety net into a framework embracing mental and cognitive conditions, caregivers and all Singapore residents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The current amendments modernise and strengthen that system.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: But as we look ahead, we must ensure that CareShield Life continues to evolve from purely a financial safety net into a comprehensive framework of care and dignity – one that embraces mental and cognitive conditions, supports caregivers and includes all who call Singapore home.

sections.label: CareShield Life payouts and premium support
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill, noting CareShield Life payouts will grow 4% yearly from 2026 to 2030 and welcoming $570 million in premium support.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my suggestions, Mr Speaker, Sir, I support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: From 2026 to 2030, payouts under CareShield Life will grow at 4% a year, which means that a new claimant in 2030 can expect about $806 a month, a meaningful step-up to keep pace with rising long-term care costs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: To cushion the impact on households, I welcome the Government’s commitment of $570 million in additional premium support over five years, which will help moderate the premium increases for workers and families who are already managing higher everyday expenses.

sections.label: Severe disability age range
sections.summary: Severe disability can strike in mid-life as well as old age, with claimants ranging from 30 to 93 and a median age of 52.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Severe disability can strike in mid-life as well as old age; claimants have ranged from 30 to 93, with a median age of 52.

sections.label: Single assessment for related schemes
sections.summary: A single severe-disability assessment ought to open the door to related schemes like the Home Caregiving Grant without repeated forms and revisits.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: A single severe-disability assessment ought to open the door to related schemes, such as the Home Caregiving Grant, without repeated forms and revisits.

sections.label: Caregiver priorities in Malay/Muslim families
sections.summary: The passage urges flexible work, a one-stop service for assessment and grants, and return-to-work pathways to support caregivers in Malay/Muslim families.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In many Malay/Muslim families, caregiving duties are shouldered by working family members, including the women, in addition to raising children and supporting parents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Daily costs, such as transport, adult diapers and follow-up treatment, can rise quickly, and the mental stress of caregivers often goes unnoticed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Therefore, three priorities must be given urgency: flexible work as the norm so that caregivers can remain employed; a "one-stop" service for assessment, grants, such as the Home Caregiving Grant, and community services; and pathways to return to work through training credits, job placement and CPF support so that retirement needs are not affected.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: These measures improve access, lighten the burden and protect the mental well-being of caregivers. : Sir, in conclusion, if we get the "3As" right, affordability with fair help and clear cost signals, adequacy that keeps pace with real pressures and is anchored by a respected care workforce, and accessibility that is simpler, faster and kinder, then seniors in our older estates like mine and caregivers across Singapore can face the future with dignity and confidence.

sections.label: Cut-off age for CareShield Life
sections.summary: The speaker asks what policy considerations were behind limiting CareShield Life coverage to those aged 30 years and older.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: While I can understand every policy needs a cut-off age, I would like to ask what the policy considerations were behind limiting CareShield Life coverage to those aged 30 years and older.

sections.label: Expanding CareShield Life coverage age
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOH to expand CareShield Life coverage to all adults from 21, with manual application for those aged 16 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: While DPS and CareShield Life serve different purposes, the minimum age for coverage for debilitating injuries should be harmonised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I therefore urge MOH to consider expanding CareShield Life coverage to all adults from 21 years of age, with an option for manual application for those aged 16 and above.

sections.label: CareShield Life coverage and premiums
sections.summary: Expanding CareShield Life coverage to more adults could lower overall risk and keep premiums affordable, and the speaker supports doubling the payout growth rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Expanding CareShield Life coverage to more adults could also have potential advantage of lowering overall risk, helping therefore to keep premiums affordable to everyone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I support the proposal to double the CareShield Life payout growth rate.

sections.label: Insurance literacy and consumer knowledge
sections.summary: The CPF Board has a Health Insurance Planner, and the speaker urges MOH to work with the Consumers Association to study and improve insurance literacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In fact, the CPF Board has an entire toolkit, called the Health Insurance Planner, to try and help policyholders cut through "the sheer volume of conflicting advice that makes it hard to know what to trust." We must do more to improve insurance literacy and help consumers save on their healthcare bills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I urge MOH to work closely with the Consumers Association of Singapore to study insurance literacy in Singapore and to work on improving consumer knowledge about how to best safeguard themselves against sudden, unintended, healthcare expenses.

sections.label: Premium increases and government subsidies
sections.summary: Higher payouts must be backed by corresponding premium increase rates to be sustainable, and the speaker welcomes government premium subsidies for policyholders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To be sustainable in the long term, higher payouts have to be backed by corresponding premium increase rates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, the Government's transitional support for policyholders in the form of premium subsidies, is welcomed.

sections.label: CareShield Life active claimants 2024
sections.summary: As of 2024, there were 1,821 active claimants under CareShield Life, aged 30 to 93, with about half in their 30s and 40s.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As of 2024, there were 1,821 active claimants under CareShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The age of the claimants ranged from 30 to 93, with about half of them in their 30s and 40s.

sections.label: Doubling payout growth and premium support
sections.summary: The decision to double payout growth to 4% until 2030 is bold and prudent, and $570 million in additional premium support shows low- and middle-income families will not be left behind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The decision to double payout growth to 4% until 2030 is both bold and prudent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Government's $570 million in additional premium support also sends a clear message – as we enhance the scheme, we will not leave low- and middle-income families behind.

sections.label: Amendment changes disability threshold test
sections.summary: The amendment replaces the threshold of being "not severely disabled" with a new statutory test of being "not disabled," a difference that can be significant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The amendment replaces the earlier threshold of being "not severely disabled" with a new statutory test of being "not disabled." The difference may seem subtle, but it can be significant.

sections.label: Fourth Schedule ADL definition
sections.summary: The Bill codifies in the new Fourth Schedule that a person is not disabled only if they can perform all six ADLs without assistance, all the time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill codifies in the new Fourth Schedule that a person is "not disabled" only if they can perform all six ADLs without assistance, all the time.

sections.label: Email service consent rules
sections.summary: Email service is allowed only with written consent, or if the person replies after being clearly informed that a reply counts as consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Email service is only allowed with written consent, or if the person replies to an email after being clearly informed that such a reply counts as consent.

sections.label: Assurance on lapsed policies
sections.summary: The question asks the Senior Minister of State to assure the House that no policy will lapse while a senior clarifies a discrepancy or appeals a premium issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Most critically, can the Senior Minister of State assure this House that no policy will lapse while a senior is still clarifying a discrepancy or appealing a premium issue?

sections.label: Payout indexing beyond 2030
sections.summary: The question asks how payouts will be indexed beyond 2030, noting 4% payout growth until 2030 gives citizens near-term confidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Fourth, Mr Speaker, Sir, looking ahead, the 4% payout growth until 2030 gives citizens confidence for the near term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State share how payouts will be indexed beyond 2030?

sections.label: Commitment to compassion in Bill
sections.summary: The passage calls for commitment as Government, community and people to ensure the Bill's compassion is felt in every assessment, letter and act of care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Let us commit, as Government, as community, as people, to ensure the compassion we enshrine in this Bill is felt in every assessment, every letter and every act of care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen
sentences.text: I said earlier that payouts would grow from $731 monthly in 2026.

sections.label: Long-term care support enhancements
sections.summary: From next year, long-term care recipients and caregivers will receive further support through enhancements to Home Caregiving Grant and long-term care subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: From next year, long-term care recipients and their caregivers will also enjoy further support for long-term care, through enhancements to Home Caregiving Grant and long-term care subsidies.

sections.label: CareShield Life payout growth recommendation
sections.summary: The CareShield Life Council recommended doubling the payout growth rate from 2% to 4% per annum to cushion rising long-term care costs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The CareShield Life Council had recommended doubling the payout growth rate from 2% to 4% per annum to allow payouts to more meaningfully cushion against rising long-term care costs.

sections.label: MediSave premium payment and ADLs
sections.summary: Premiums can be paid using MediSave up to annual withdrawal limits, as the ADLs construct objectively measures caregiving assistance needed regardless of underlying conditions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The premiums for these can also be paid for using MediSave, up to the annual withdrawal limits.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: This is because the ADLs construct is an objective measure of the level of caregiving assistance that a patient requires, regardless of the underlying conditions.

sections.label: Optional coverage and adverse selection
sections.summary: Extending CareShield Life coverage optionally to those aged 16 and above would lead to adverse selection, as those more likely to claim would opt in.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: If we extend CareShield Life coverage to those aged 16 and above on an optional basis, this will lead to adverse selection where those who are more likely to make claims are more likely to opt in.

sections.label: Premium increase and support
sections.summary: A one-step premium increase in 2026 then 4% annually is needed, with $570 million in support moderating 2026 to 2030 increases to $38 average and no more than $75.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: To support the increase in payout growth rate, there needs to be a one-step increase in premiums in 2026, followed by 4% increase per annum thereafter.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Given that the one-step increase is something that may be of concern to policyholders, we are providing an additional $570 million in premium support to cushion the increase for all policyholders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: With this support, annual premium increases from 2026 to 2030 are moderated to $38 on average and no more than $75.

sections.label: Matched MediSave Scheme
sections.summary: The Government will introduce the Matched MediSave Scheme from 2026, with 1:1 matching for voluntary cash top-ups up to $1,000 yearly for those with lower MediSave balances.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The Government will also be introducing the Matched MediSave Scheme from 2026, with 1:1 Government matching for voluntary cash top-ups of up to $1,000 per year, for those with lower MediSave balances.

sections.label: Life expectancy for women and men
sections.summary: In 2024, average life expectancy was 85.6 years for women compared to 81.2 years for men.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The average life expectancy for women is 85.6 years in 2024 compared to 81.2 years for men.

sections.label: CareShield Life Optional Cohort enrolment
sections.summary: About 900,000 Optional Cohort individuals enrolled by June 2025, and new applications fell almost 90%, so underwriting criteria return from 1 January 2026.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: As of June 2025, about 900,000 individuals in the Optional Cohort, or about half of the cohort, have enrolled in CareShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: As shared in my opening speech, new CareShield Life applications from the Optional Cohort have decreased by almost 90% compared to when the scheme was first launched.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Most Optional Cohort individuals who wanted to join CareShield Life would have already done so by now.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Hence, the CareShield Life Council has assessed that it is timely to reinstate the planned underwriting criteria from 1 January 2026 onwards.

sections.label: Serving documents electronically
sections.summary: The Bill's provisions let important documents be served to policyholders through additional modalities, including electronic means.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Specifically, the provisions in the Bill enable us to serve important documents to policyholders through additional modalities, including electronic means.

sections.label: MediShield Life premium discounts
sections.summary: Eligible Singaporeans in healthy lifestyle programmes and challenges get discounts of up to $580 off MediShield Life premiums yearly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Eligible Singaporeans participating in healthy lifestyle programmes and challenges will be rewarded with discounts of up to $580 off their MediShield Life premiums per year.

sections.label: Severe disability assessor numbers
sections.summary: Since CareShield Life launched, severe disability assessors island-wide doubled from over 300 to more than 700.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Since CareShield Life was launched, we have doubled the number of severe disability assessors island-wide from over 300 at launch to now more than 700 assessors.

sections.label: Clinical reviews and AIC Link offices
sections.summary: Assessment outcomes are subject to further clinical reviews if necessary, and there are now nine AIC Link offices island-wide.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: These assessment outcomes are also subject to further clinical reviews, if necessary.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We now have nine AIC Link offices across the island.

sections.label: CareShield Life support and Bill
sections.summary: The Bill strengthens the legislative framework for CareShield Life through underwriting criteria and premium recovery mechanisms, supporting long-term care subsidies and payouts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Financially, we have reviewed our support ecosystem to ensure that Singaporeans have access to affordable care through enhancements to long-term care subsidies and grants earlier this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: With the enhancements to CareShield Life, Singaporeans can be assured that these insurance payouts, too, will continue to provide meaningful support for long-term care, should they need it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The Council will continue to review the scheme to ensure that it remains relevant to policyholders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: This Bill supports these enhancements by strengthening the legislative framework to ensure that the scheme remains fair and sustainable through appropriate underwriting criteria and enhanced premium recovery mechanisms.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: These amendments will help ensure that CareShield Life continues to provide essential financial protection when families need it most, for current and future generations of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Premium subsidies and coverage assurance
sections.summary: The Minister assures that Singapore Citizens who cannot pay premiums will be fully covered through additional premium subsidies, with no lapse in CareShield Life payouts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: So, I hope the Senior Minister of State understand that it is still relevant.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But let me just say that the biggest assurance from my speech today that the Member should take back is that, under whatever circumstances, if a Singapore Citizen cannot pay any part of the premiums needed, we will cover fully whatever is needed through the additional premium subsidies to make sure that no one is without coverage for CareShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In the instance if there is any premium that is owed, we will not hold back the disbursement of support that is needed for this individual and talk about the recovery of the premiums that may take place at some point in time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But we will act with compassion and make sure that the person who needs the payout from CareShield Life will not have a lapse of payment from CareShield Life in any instance.

sections.label: Gender neutral premiums and claims data
sections.summary: The Leader of the Opposition in 2018 raised gender neutral premiums, and the Minister says claims data is not mature enough for robust conclusions.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: And, in fact, this was a point that was raised in 2018 by the Leader of the Opposition when he actually stated, noting at the same time the then-health Government Parliamentary Committee Chair had also called for how we can move towards gender neutral premiums, and Mr Singh at that time also said that it would mean men will pay more and women less, let it be so.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I think this CareShield Life is barely about five years and as I said earlier, many of the policyholders today are still quite young and the claims data is, at this point, not mature enough for us to draw any robust conclusions.

sections.label: Premium drop for Optional Cohort
sections.summary: The Optional Cohort will see a premium drop from next year once underwriting criteria are tightened, as they no longer pay for peers joining with disability.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Which means that the burden will be shared by a lesser number of people in terms of premiums that need to keep the funds for that cohort for claims sustainable.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And that is why the premium will be higher and once we tighten the reins and reinstate the original underwriting criteria, as I mentioned in my speech earlier, the Optional Cohort who are still policyholders today will see a premium drop from next year onwards because they now do not have to pay higher premium to account for some of the peers who may suddenly join in with disability that may draw down on the claims.

sections.label: Tightening underwriting and sign-in period
sections.summary: The sign-in period was extended from two to four years with up to $4,000 in premium subsidies, and underwriting will be tightened to be fair to existing Optional Cohort policyholders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And that is what their cohort has been bearing for the last few years before we now make this move to tighten the underwriting criteria.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And we have actually extended the sign-in period from two years to four years to give ample time and double our outreach efforts as well to encourage those who may want to consider to come in to join the scheme before the end of this year, including availing up to $4,000 of premium subsidies to make it more as a reassurance that when they come in there will be premium subsidies to make it affordable for the Optional Cohort to join in.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, given that the number who are signing up now has dropped down to a lower number, we think this is about time to tighten the underwriting to make sure it is fair to the other existing policyholders who are in the Optional Cohort that has already come in for the last few years.

sections.label: Partial system risks gaming
sections.summary: The Minister says a partial system would be difficult to construct as it would open things to gaming and adverse selection, making the scheme unsustainable.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Have I answered all the Member's three questions?

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I would say that will be a very difficult thing to construct because once you have a partial kind of system that is neither here nor there, not very clearcut, you would open things to gaming, to adverse selection and that will make the whole scheme unsustainable.

sections.label: Scoring system and disability coverage
sections.summary: The CareShield Life Council considered broadening coverage beyond severe disability but took the approach that this would impact premiums and affordability for other policyholders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: On the scoring system, the crux of the issue is whether we want to allow those with moderate, maybe even mild, disability to be included and that means expanding the scope of coverage.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Because if you are taking a graded approach, it means that you are trying to define those who are lesser than severe disability according to today's ADL definition, to be assessable for claims.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: That means broadening the coverage to a wider pool of people which must mean that the payouts must increase, which must mean that premium loading on existing cohorts must go up.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The CareShield Life Council did consider whether we should broaden from beyond severe disability to those with more moderate disability.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But I think in the end, the Council took the approach that that would mean that there will be policy premium impacts on the rest of the policyholders and potentially make it less affordable to more Singaporeans.

sections.label: CareShield Life disability assessment scoring
sections.summary: The passage explains that using the modified Barthel Index limits CareShield Life support to those with severe disability, aligning with international practice and sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: An individual reporting maximal assistance in three areas, let us say toileting, bathing and dressing, for instance but be able to fully perform all other functions – so this is someone that would fully qualify for CareShield Life – would score 80 points on the modified Barthel Index, which is actually a higher score that another individual who requires just moderate assistance in, for example, transferring mobility, dressing and feeding and yet be able to perform other functions independently.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: So, my point is that when you use a scoring system, it is not necessarily the case that you immediately will expand to a much larger pool of individuals but actually just those individuals that truly need the assistance to disability.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I understand there are different assessment tools in the market in assessing disability but what we are choosing to use is something is widely adopted at the World Health Organization, in the European Union, widely used by insurers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I think it is something that we want to do, that it is aligned with international practice, that is also easy and convenient for our assessors and our clinicians to use, rather than put in different matrixes that actually ends up promulgating different tools and creating some confusion.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I think we both agree that we should try to make sure that the scheme is sustainable at this moment as far as CareShield Life is concerned, to limit the support to those with severe disability.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Those at the margins, we will take a compassionate approach.
